title: Windows PCs (desktops and laptops)
description: Bench repair checklist for Windows desktops and laptops, ordered from the most common faults (intake damage, power, storage and software) to deeper hardware diagnostics. All-in-ones and mini PCs can use it too; items carry notes where they differ.

references.title: Dell Support (service tag lookup, diagnostics, drivers)

safety: Shut down and unplug before opening the case. On laptops, disconnect the internal battery connector before working on the board.
Use ESD precautions (grounded wrist strap, or touch bare grounded metal) before handling RAM, drives, cards or the motherboard.
Never open a power supply or a laptop charger. Their capacitors can hold a dangerous charge after unplugging.
Swollen or damaged lithium batteries can catch fire. Don't press, bend or puncture them; store removed batteries in a fire-safe container.
Get the customer's OK and a backup before anything that can erase data: a reinstall, a drive swap, or a BIOS/TPM reset with BitLocker on.

sections.title: 1. Intake and visible damage
sections.description: Confirm the complaint and look before you power on.

items.title: Reproduce the reported fault
items.check: Get the customer's description, any error messages and when it started. Reproduce it before changing anything and note exactly what you saw.
items.signs: Can't reproduce it: ask for steps, a photo of the error or when it happens. It may end as No fault found.

items.title: Customer data, sign-in and encryption
items.check: Ask whether the data matters and is backed up. Record how you'll sign in (PIN/password arrangement) and whether BitLocker or device encryption is on; get the recovery key before touching the BIOS, TPM or drive.
items.fix: Back up first when the drive is failing or a reinstall is likely. Image a failing drive before running long scans on it.

items.title: Case, hinge and port damage
items.check: Look for cracks, dents, broken hinges, loose bezels, bent or loose ports, and missing screws or feet. Photograph existing damage at intake.
items.signs: Drop damage, lid that won't stay up, ports that only work at an angle.
items.otherSeries: All-in-ones: also check the stand, rear cover clips and the screen glass.

items.title: Liquid damage or corrosion
items.check: Look for sticky keys, residue, water stains, corrosion on ports and screws, and tripped liquid contact indicators.
items.fix: Don't power on a wet unit. Disconnect the battery, disassemble, clean with isopropyl alcohol and inspect under chips and connectors for corrosion.

items.title: Swollen battery
items.check: Look for a raised touchpad, a lifted keyboard, a bulging bottom cover or gaps opening along the case seams.
items.fix: Stop. Don't press or puncture it. Remove the battery, store it in a fire-safe container and replace it.

items.title: Burn marks, melted plastic or smell
items.check: Inspect the power socket, charger, charging port, PSU and motherboard power connectors. Smell for burnt electronics.
items.fix: Find the source before powering on. Replace any scorched cable, charger, PSU or board.

items.title: Charger and accessories received
items.check: Record what came in: charger (wattage and part number), cables, dock, external drives, peripherals. Note anything missing.

sections.title: 2. Power and startup
sections.description: Won't turn on, turns off, or no picture at startup.

items.title: Outlet, power cable and power strip
items.check: Try a known-good outlet and power cable. Bypass power strips, UPS units and surge protectors.

items.title: Power adapter / charger
items.check: Check the charger's wattage matches the original, its LED lights, the barrel tip or USB-C end isn't damaged, and the output with a meter or USB-C power meter.
items.signs: Charges slowly, "plugged in, not charging", slow-charger warning, shuts off under load.
items.fix: Swap in a known-good charger of the same or higher wattage.
items.otherSeries: All-in-ones and mini PCs often use a laptop-style external brick; test it the same way.

items.title: Power supply (PSU)
items.check: Rear switch on, voltage selector (if fitted) correct, PSU fan spins. Test with a PSU tester or a known-good PSU, and check the 24-pin and CPU 8-pin connectors are fully seated.
items.signs: Completely dead, clicking, random restarts under load, burning smell.
items.fix: Replace with a unit of equal or higher wattage and the right connectors. Don't open the PSU.

items.title: Drain residual power / embedded controller reset
items.check: Unplug power (and disconnect the battery on laptops), hold the power button for 30 seconds, then retry. Laptops: also try the maker's EC reset (pinhole or key combination) if it has one.
items.signs: No response at all after a power cut, a dead battery or a sleep that never woke up.

items.title: Beep codes, diagnostic LEDs and error lights
items.check: Note any beeps, blinking power or charging LED patterns, and motherboard debug LEDs or codes (CPU, DRAM, VGA, BOOT). Look them up for this make and model.
items.fix: The code usually points at the part to test next: RAM, CPU, graphics or the board.

items.title: Power button and front panel
items.check: Check the power button clicks and its cable is seated (front-panel header on desktops, button ribbon on laptops). Desktops: briefly short the PWR pins to rule out the button.

items.title: Random shutdowns or restarts
items.check: Check Event Viewer for Kernel-Power 41 and WHEA-Logger errors and when they happen. Reproduce under load while watching temperatures.
items.signs: Turns off under load (heat or PSU), restarts with no warning, shuts off on battery at a set percentage.
items.fix: Under load → check cooling and the PSU/charger. WHEA errors → test RAM, CPU and temperatures.

sections.title: 3. Storage and boot drive
sections.description: Behind most "slow PC" and "won't boot" complaints.

items.title: Boot drive detected in BIOS/UEFI
items.check: Enter BIOS/UEFI setup and confirm the boot drive is listed and first in the boot order. Check the boot mode (UEFI vs Legacy/CSM) and that the storage mode (AHCI vs RAID/RST/VMD) hasn't changed.
items.signs: "No bootable device", "Boot device not found", goes straight into the BIOS.

items.title: Drive health (SMART)
items.check: Read SMART with CrystalDiskInfo, the drive maker's tool or the built-in diagnostics. Look at reallocated and pending sectors, CRC errors, NVMe percentage used and media errors.
items.signs: Very slow, freezes for seconds, clicking hard drive, corrupt files, long boot times.
items.fix: Caution or Bad: back up or clone now, then replace. Moving a hard-drive PC to an SSD fixes most "slow" complaints.

items.title: Free space on the system drive
items.check: Check C: has at least 10–15% free. Look for large Downloads, temp files, Windows.old and update caches.
items.fix: Disk Cleanup (including system files) or Storage Sense, move user data off, or fit a larger drive.

items.title: Drive cables and seating
items.check: Reseat SATA data and power cables, or the M.2 drive and its screw. Try another SATA port and cable. A rising CRC error count points at the cable or connection.

items.title: Windows startup repair
items.check: If the drive is healthy but Windows won't start: try Startup Repair, Safe Mode, System Restore and uninstalling the latest update from the recovery environment, then bootrec / bcdboot if needed.
items.signs: Boot loop, stuck on "Preparing Automatic Repair", INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE.

items.title: BitLocker recovery prompt
items.check: If it asks for a BitLocker recovery key, get it from the customer's Microsoft account or their IT department. Don't wipe a drive that asks for a key without the customer's consent.
items.signs: Recovery prompt after a BIOS update, TPM reset, board swap or boot-order change.

sections.title: 4. Windows and software
sections.description: The usual cause of "slow", "pop-ups" and "keeps crashing".

items.title: Startup apps and background load
items.check: In Task Manager, check CPU, memory and disk use at idle, and the Startup apps list for things that don't need to run.
items.fix: Disable unneeded startup apps and remove bundled trial software.

items.title: Malware and unwanted software
items.check: Run a full Microsoft Defender scan (Defender Offline if anything looks off). Review installed programs, browser extensions, homepage/search settings and scheduled tasks.
items.signs: Pop-ups, search redirects, unknown programs, high CPU from unknown processes, ransom notes.
items.fix: Remove and rescan. Ransomware: disconnect it from the network and stop; let the customer decide before anything is wiped.

items.title: Device Manager errors and drivers
items.check: Look for devices with warning icons or "Unknown device". Check chipset, graphics, storage, network and audio drivers come from the PC or part maker.
items.fix: Install drivers from the maker's support site using the service tag or serial.

items.title: Windows Update
items.check: Check for pending, failed or stuck updates, and that this Windows version is still supported.
items.fix: Run the Windows Update troubleshooter, clear the SoftwareDistribution cache, or install the latest cumulative update manually.

items.title: Blue screens and app crashes
items.check: Check Reliability Monitor and Event Viewer, and read minidumps in C:\Windows\Minidump for the stop code and the driver named.
items.signs: Blue screens (BSOD), apps closing, "not responding".
items.fix: A driver is named → update or roll it back. Memory or WHEA errors → test RAM and temperatures.

items.title: System file check
items.check: As administrator run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth, then sfc /scannow, and note what each reports.
items.fix: If both keep failing, an in-place upgrade (repair install) keeps apps and files while replacing Windows.

items.title: User profile and sign-in
items.check: Can the user sign in normally? Look for a temporary profile, a corrupted profile, a forgotten PIN or password, or a Microsoft account sign-in problem.

items.title: Windows activation and licences
items.check: Settings → Activation shows Windows is activated, and Office and other paid software are licensed.
items.signs: "Activate Windows" watermark after a motherboard swap or reinstall.

items.title: Dust in fans, heatsinks and vents
items.check: Look into the intake and exhaust vents and heatsink fins for dust mats and pet hair.
items.fix: Blow out with compressed air while holding fans still. Open the case or bottom cover for heavy build-up.

items.title: Fans spinning and quiet
items.check: Confirm every fan spins (CPU, case, graphics card, laptop blower). Listen for grinding, clicking or rattling.
items.fix: Clean, reseat the fan connector, or replace a noisy or failed fan.

items.title: CPU and GPU temperatures under load
items.check: Watch temperatures and clock speeds (HWiNFO or similar) at idle and during a 10-minute stress test. Look for thermal throttling.
items.signs: Hot to the touch, loud fans, slows down after a few minutes, shuts off under load.
items.fix: Clean first. If temperatures stay high, repaste and check the heatsink is mounted evenly.

items.title: Thermal paste and pads
items.check: On older or overheating units, inspect the CPU/GPU paste (dried out or pumped out) and the pads on memory and power components.
items.fix: Clean with isopropyl alcohol and repaste. Replace pads with the same thickness.

items.title: Liquid cooler pump and leaks
items.check: Pump running (pump header shows RPM, you can feel or hear it), no leaks on the tubes or block, radiator fans spinning.
items.signs: CPU overheats within seconds of booting, gurgling noises, coolant residue.

items.title: RAM seated in the right slots
items.check: Reseat the modules. On desktops, use the slots the motherboard manual recommends for dual channel (usually A2 and B2).
items.signs: Fans run but no picture, DRAM debug LED, memory beep code.
items.fix: Reseat, clean the contacts, then try one module at a time in each slot.
items.otherSeries: Thin laptops and some mini PCs have memory soldered to the board; it can't be reseated or replaced separately.

items.title: Memory test
items.check: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic or MemTest86 for at least one full pass. Note any errors and which module.
items.signs: Random blue screens (MEMORY_MANAGEMENT, PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA), corrupt files, failed installs.
items.fix: Replace the failing module. If errors only appear with XMP/EXPO on, run the memory at default speed.

items.title: Enough memory for the workload
items.check: Compare installed memory with what's in use in Task Manager → Performance during normal work.
items.signs: Memory near 100% with a browser and a few apps open; slow switching between apps.
items.fix: Upgrade with a matching type and speed, or reduce what runs at once.

items.title: Test with an external monitor
items.check: Connect a known-good monitor. Picture on the external screen but not the built-in one points at the panel, its cable or the backlight; nothing on either points at graphics, RAM or the board.

items.title: Monitor, cable and input
items.check: Check the monitor's input source, and try another cable and port. With a graphics card fitted, plug into the card, not the motherboard.

items.title: Screen damage, lines and backlight
items.check: Look for cracks, lines, dead pixels and flicker when moving the lid. Shine a flashlight at a dark screen: a faint image means the backlight has failed.
items.fix: Lines or flicker that change as the hinge moves → display cable. Cracks or lines that don't → replace the panel (match the part number and connector).

items.title: Graphics card seating and power
items.check: Reseat the card, check its PCIe power cables are fully in, the slot latch clicks and the card isn't sagging. Look for artifacts during a GPU stress test.
items.signs: Artifacts, "display driver stopped responding", black screen under load.

items.title: Graphics driver
items.check: Use the current driver from the PC maker or the GPU vendor. If problems started after an update, roll back or do a clean install.

items.title: Keyboard
items.check: Test every key with a key tester. Look for stuck, dead or double-typing keys and a working backlight.
items.fix: Clean under the keys. Liquid damage or several dead keys usually means replacing the keyboard (often part of the top case).

items.title: Touchpad
items.check: Test pointer movement, clicks and gestures, and that it isn't turned off with an Fn key or in Settings.
items.signs: A raised or stiff touchpad can mean a swollen battery underneath.

items.title: Charging port / DC jack
items.check: Wiggle the charger plug gently: does charging cut in and out? Look for a loose, burnt or bent jack or USB-C port.
items.fix: Replace the DC jack or USB-C port board. Some are soldered to the motherboard.

items.title: USB and other ports
items.check: Test each USB-A and USB-C port with a known-good device. Check for loose or bent ports, and USB-C charging and display output where supported.

items.title: Speakers, headphone jack and microphone
items.check: Play audio through the speakers and headphones and record with the microphone. Check the right input and output devices are selected.

items.title: Webcam
items.check: Open the Camera app. Check the privacy shutter or camera key, and camera permissions in Settings.

items.title: Wi-Fi connects and stays connected
items.check: Connect to a known network, check signal and speed, and that Airplane mode or a Wi-Fi switch isn't on.
items.fix: Update or reinstall the Wi-Fi driver, or use Network reset. Weak signal after a repair: check the antenna cables are connected.

items.title: Wired Ethernet
items.check: Plug in a known-good cable: link light on, gets an IP address, reaches the internet.

items.title: Bluetooth
items.check: Pair a known device. Check the Bluetooth adapter shows in Device Manager without errors.

items.title: Battery health and wear
items.check: Run powercfg /batteryreport and compare full charge capacity with design capacity. Note the cycle count.
items.signs: Short runtime, dies suddenly at a set percentage, won't charge past a level.
items.fix: Replace when well worn (roughly below 60–70% of design capacity). Check for a charge limit setting (e.g. 80% battery care) before replacing.

items.title: Charges and reports correctly
items.check: Charging light and Windows both show charging, the percentage rises steadily, and it runs on battery when unplugged.

sections.title: 11. Motherboard, BIOS and hardware diagnostics
sections.description: Deeper checks when the earlier sections haven't found it.

items.title: Maker's built-in hardware diagnostics
items.check: Run the maker's diagnostics (Dell ePSA / SupportAssist, HP PC Hardware Diagnostics, Lenovo Diagnostics, or the motherboard's BIOS tests) and note any error codes.

items.title: BIOS/UEFI version and settings
items.check: Note the BIOS version and compare with the latest from the maker. Check date and time, boot mode, Secure Boot and TPM status.
items.fix: Update only on stable power (laptop charger connected and battery charged). Suspend BitLocker first. Load defaults if settings were changed.

items.title: CMOS battery
items.check: Wrong date and time after unplugging, or a "CMOS checksum" message, means the coin cell is flat.
items.fix: Replace the coin cell (often a CR2032), then set the date, time and BIOS settings again.

items.title: Board damage and shorts
items.check: With the board visible, look for bulging or leaking capacitors, burnt components, corrosion, bent CPU socket pins (desktops) and stray screws or standoffs touching the board.

items.title: Minimal-configuration boot test
items.check: Strip down to motherboard, CPU and cooler, one RAM module and the PSU (on the bench if needed). Add parts back one at a time until the fault returns.

items.title: Original complaint fixed
items.check: Repeat the steps that reproduced the fault and confirm it no longer happens.

items.title: Stress / burn-in test
items.check: Run a CPU and GPU stress test for 15–30 minutes. Temperatures stay in range with no errors, restarts or throttling.

items.title: Updates and security left current
items.check: Windows Update finished with no pending restart, Microsoft Defender (or the customer's antivirus) on and up to date.

items.title: Customer data and accounts intact
items.check: Spot-check the customer's files, email and key apps open. Remove any temporary admin accounts, tools or bench files you added.

items.title: Reassembly and cleanup
items.check: All screws back, covers clipped in fully, no rattles, rubber feet on, and the unit cleaned (screen, keyboard, case).
